items.title: Section: Mind's Twenty States Close; Phenomena-Mindfulness Opens

items.zh: 不掉心者，謂於舉時及於略時得平等捨。寂靜心者，謂從諸蓋已得解脫。不寂靜心者，謂從諸蓋未得解脫言。定心者，謂從諸蓋得解脫已，復能證入根本靜慮。不定心者，謂未能入。善修心者，謂於此定長時串習，得隨所欲、得無艱難、得無梗澁，速能證入。不善修心者，與此相違，應知其相。善解脫心者，謂從一切，究竟解脫。不善解脫心者，謂不從一切不究竟解脫。如是十四種心，當知皆是住時所起。依淨蓋地住時所起，有八種心。謂從略心、散心、乃至寂靜、不寂靜心。依淨煩惱地住時所起，有六種心。謂定心、不定心、乃至善解脫、不善解脫心。又於內有蓋，能自了知我有諸蓋；於內無蓋，能自了知我無諸蓋。如彼諸蓋未生而生，亦能了知；如彼諸蓋生已散滅，亦能了知。於眼有結乃至於意有結，能自了知我有眼結乃至我有意結；於眼無結乃至於意無結，能自了知我眼無結乃至我意無結。如彼眼結乃至意結未生而生，亦能了知；如彼諸結生已散滅，亦能了知。
items.en: An unagitated mind is one that has found even equanimity, whether lifted or contracted. A tranquil mind is one liberated from the hindrances. … A concentrated mind is one that, having been liberated from the hindrances, is further able to enter the fundamental absorptions. … A well-liberated mind is one liberated from everything, finally and completely. A not-yet-well-liberated mind is one not yet liberated from everything, not yet finally. These fourteen states of mind should all be understood as arising during seated practice. Further: when a hindrance is present within, one knows for oneself, "I have this hindrance"; when none is present, one knows for oneself, "I have no such hindrance." One likewise knows when a hindrance not yet arisen comes to arise, and when a hindrance, having arisen, then dissolves away.

items.title: Section: The Four Foundations of Mindfulness Close in Full

items.zh: 於內有念等覺支，能自了知我有念等覺支；於內無念等覺支，能自了知我無念等覺支。如念等覺支未生而生，亦能了知；如生已住，不忘修滿，倍復修習，增長廣大，亦能了知。如念等覺支，如是擇法、精進、喜、安、定、捨等覺支，當知亦爾。若能如是如實遍知諸雜染法自性、因緣、過患、對治，是為法念住體。如說於身住循身觀，念及念住。如是於受、於心、於法，隨其所應，當知亦爾。
items.en: When mindfulness and the other factors of enlightenment are present within, one knows for oneself, "I have them"; when absent, one knows, "I do not." One likewise knows when they arise not having arisen before, and, once arisen and abiding, knows that they are not forgotten, are brought to completion, doubled in practice, and made to grow vast. Being able, in this way, to thoroughly and truly know the intrinsic nature, causes and conditions, faults, and antidote of every defiled state — this is the essential nature of phenomena-mindfulness. Just as has been said of dwelling in observation of the body, and of mindfulness and its establishment there — so too, adjusted as fitting to each, should the same be understood for feeling, mind, and phenomena.

items.zh: 云何於內身等住循身等觀？云何於外身等住循身等觀？云何於內外身等住循身等觀？謂若緣內自有情數身色為境，住循身觀，是名於內身住循身觀。若緣外非有情數色為境，住循身觀，是名於外身住循身觀。若緣外他有情數身色為境，住循身觀，是名於內外身住循身觀。若緣依內自有情數身色所生受、心、法為境，住循三觀；是名於內受、心、法住循受、心、法觀。若緣依外非有情數色所生受、心、法為境，住循三觀，是名於外受、心、法住循受心法觀。若緣依外他有情數身色所生受、心、法為境，住循三觀，是名於內外受、心、法住循受心法觀。復有差別。謂若緣根所攝、有執有受色為境，是名於內身住循身觀。若緣非根所攝、無執無受色為境，是名於外身住循身觀。若緣非根所攝、有執有受色為境，是名於內外身住循身觀。如是若緣依前三色所生受、心、法為境，隨其所應，當知即是住循三觀。

blocks.text: The last states of mind, mindfulness of phenomena, and what "internal", "external", and "both" mean. A passage at 0441a16 is untranslated.

"An unagitated mind is one that has found even equanimity. A tranquil mind is one liberated from the hindrances. A concentrated mind is one that, having been prepared, is absorbed. A well-cultivated mind; a well-liberated mind."

Mindfulness of phenomena: the hindrances and the factors of awakening. "When mindfulness and the other factors of awakening are present within, one knows for oneself, 'I have them'; when absent, 'I do not'." One knows how they arise, how they are maintained. "Being able, in this way, to truly know their intrinsic nature, causes and conditions, faults, and antidotes": that is dwelling in observation of phenomena.

What do "internal", "external", and "internal-external" mean? First reading: one's own body is internal; non-living matter external; another being's body is "internal-external". The same for the feeling, mind, and phenomena based on each. Second reading: matter that belongs to the sense faculties and is appropriated by consciousness is internal; matter that is neither is external; matter appropriated by consciousness but not a faculty (the faculties' supports, the flesh) is internal-external.

The *Satipaṭṭhāna* formula, "internally, externally, and both", has puzzled many readers. The treatise offers precise readings. The point is that mindfulness is not only of "my" body and mind; it extends to everything experienced.

quiz.q: What is the essential nature of phenomena-mindfulness?
options: truly knowing the nature, conditions, faults, and antidotes of every defiled state
quiz.why: "Being able, in this way, to thoroughly and truly know the intrinsic nature, causes and conditions, faults, and antidote of every defiled state — this is the essential nature of phenomena-mindfulness." Master Cháng Bǎi: truly and fully knowing the defiled states in one's mind — each one's nature, the conditions that produce it, its faults, and how to counter it.

quiz.q: Phenomena-mindfulness notes whether the factors of enlightenment are present. What kind of method does Venerable Miào Jìng say they are?
options: a method able to cut off the hindrances and the fetters
quiz.why: "When mindfulness and the other factors of enlightenment are present within, one knows for oneself, 'I have them'; when absent, one knows, 'I do not.'" Venerable Miào Jìng: these factors should be methods able to cut off the hindrances and the fetters.
